 US Strategic Petroleum Reserve is projected to hit a new low before rebounding in late 2027
 Ben Werschkul · Washington Correspondent Tue, November 10, 2026 at 3:58 PM EST 3 min read CL=F +0.35% 
 The US Energy Information Administration (EIA) projects that the government's Strategic Petroleum Reserve will reach new lows in the coming months due to additional Iran- and hurricane-related withdrawals before rebounding in late 2027. 
 The estimates in the EIA's new short-term energy outlook project the nation's energy backstop will bottom out at a little over 240 million barrels in the early half of next year before new deposits could push reserves up to 344.7 million barrels by the end of 2027. 
 The reserve — according to the US Department of Energy — currently sits at 279.5 million barrels as of Nov. 6. 
 The Trump administration announced plans last month to sell up to 4 million barrels of crude oil in response to Hurricane Isaias on top of ongoing sales of about 40 million barrels related to supply disruptions in the Middle East. 
 Deposits later next year would be at least partially the result of the new US relationship with Venezuela. President Trump's team has outlined a complex process ahead where new Venezuelan imports of a heavier type of oil would be traded for the light or medium United States crude oil that would then be added to the reserve. 
 Tuesday's monthly report from the EIA also shows projections of further growth in US crude oil and natural gas production over the coming year.  
 The report foresees high gas prices for the remainder of 2026 before declining in 2027 and ending next year with the spot price of Brent crude oil at $77 per barrel. 
 That could lead to declines in the US average retail price of gasoline and diesel over 2027, with the group's latest projection that retail gasoline prices will average $3.73 per gallon next year. 
 US retail gasoline prices have eased in the last week and are now below $4 per gallon . Brent Crude Oil is near $90 per barrel . 
 Historically low reserve levels 
 Energy reserves have become a pointed political issue, with some Democrats promising to press the Trump administration on the "structural integrity" of the depleted caverns that have seen steep drawdowns since the start of the Iran War. 
 The Trump administration has said that only 70 million barrels must remain in the reserve to safely manage the caverns. 
 The reserve currently sits at the lowest levels since October of 1982. Further withdrawals would push the reserve to the lowest readings on record . 
 The Strategic Petroleum Reserve storage at the Bryan Mound site is seen in 2022. (Brandon Bell/Getty Images) · Brandon Bell via Getty Images For his part, Trump has often tried to project confidence that US reserves will be quickly and cheaply refilled.  
 He told a crowd in Alabama during a campaign stop that, because of an energy deal with Venezuela, "We're going to be filling up very shortly our strategic reserves for nothing." The president this week told reporters that he believes the war in Iran "militarily is effectively over."  
 Story Continues Despite Trump's promises, experts say refilling the reserves will be a complex and costly process that could take years. 
 Even accounting for projected deposits in 2027, the reserve would remain far below the more than 600 million barrels it held as recently as 2021 before significant drawdowns both during the Biden and Trump administrations.  
 Ben Werschkul is a Washington correspondent for Yahoo Finance.
